app.name: Vitals
app.tagline: See what your computer is actually doing.

confirm.endBody: Unsaved work in this app will be lost.
confirm.endCriticalBody: Ending it will make Windows unstable and may cause a restart or data loss.
confirm.safe: Unsaved work in this app will be lost.
confirm.disruptive: This will close your desktop and any open windows. It usually restarts on its own.
confirm.critical: The system depends on this. Ending it will crash Windows immediately and you will lose unsaved work in every app.
confirm.forbidden: Windows protects this process. It cannot be ended, even as an administrator.
confirm.denied: Windows refused: this process belongs to another account or to the system. Retrying as administrator asks for approval once, for this action only.

capability.noSuchHardware: Your hardware does not report this

sampling.title: Sampling
sampling.backgroundThrottleHint: Keeps Vitals near-zero cost when you are not looking at it.

history.title: History
history.enableHint: Stored only on this computer. Off by default.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.noTelemetry: Vitals collects nothing about you and sends it nowhere.
privacy.localOnly: Everything it measures stays on this computer. History, if you turn it on, is a local file you can delete.
privacy.noCrashReports: There is no crash reporting and no usage analytics. If Vitals crashes, it writes crash.txt in its own folder for you to attach to a bug report — it never sends it.
privacy.noLookups: No file is ever hashed or looked up online.
privacy.lanServer: The LAN server for your phone and other tools is off until you turn it on, and only answers devices on your own network. A local-only connection on 127.0.0.1 is always open so the vitals command-line tool can reach the app.
privacy.updates: The only request Vitals makes by itself is an update check to GitHub, about 20 seconds after launch. GitHub sees your IP address and the app version, as with any download. Turn it off under About.

about.title: About
about.contribute: Vitals is free and open source, forever.
about.contributeBody: Found a bug or want a feature? Open an issue on GitHub — every report makes it better.

update.title: Updates
update.idle: Vitals can check GitHub for a newer version.
update.upToDate: You are running the latest version.
update.unconfigured: Updates are not configured for this build.
update.unconfiguredHint: Development and unsigned builds cannot verify an update. Download the latest release from GitHub instead.
update.autoHint: Checks GitHub shortly after launch and installs a signed update when you quit. Nothing is installed while you are using Vitals.
update.pending: Version {{version}} is downloaded and installs when you quit Vitals.

hud.title: Vitals
hud.clickThroughHint: Clicks pass through to whatever is behind. Press Ctrl+Shift+H to bring it back.

empty.title: No PC is paired yet
empty.body: On the computer you want to watch, open Vitals → Settings → Remote access, turn it on, then scan the QR code it shows with this phone's camera.
empty.pairFailedBody: The computer did not answer, or the code has expired. Show a fresh QR code on the PC and scan it again.

processes.title: Processes
processes.noneBody: No process on this computer matches what you typed.
processes.pickMachineBody: Open the Machines tab and tap the computer whose processes you want to see.

action.title: What should {{name}} do?
action.confirmHint: Tap again to confirm. Unsaved work in this app will be lost.
action.readOnlyBody: Re-pair it from the PC with control allowed if you want to end tasks from here.
action.denied: Windows would not let Vitals touch this process

settings.title: Settings
settings.themeFollows: Follows your phone's light or dark setting.
settings.pairAnotherBody: Open Vitals on that computer, go to Settings → Remote access, and scan its QR code with this phone.
